title: Beyond Simulated Benchmarks: Evaluating Motion Representations for Fall Detection Under Real-World Data Scarcity
abstract: arXiv:2608.13197v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Falls are a major health concern for older adults, and wearable sensors have been widely explored for detecting falls and enabling timely intervention. However, real-world falls are extremely rare: collecting 100 of them requires an estimated 100,000 days of monitoring, resulting in severely limited labelled data for training machine learning models. Consequently, many approaches rely on simulated datasets, often reporting high laboratory performance but limited real-world generalisation. We present a systematic evaluation of motion representations for wearable fall detection under real-world data scarcity. Using accelerometer signals, we compare interval-based, kernel-based, symbolic, and foundation model representations. As an interpretable baseline, we additionally investigate a lightweight symbolic representation that converts short motion segments into symbolic sentences augmented with physically-grounded impact descriptors. translated_title: 超越模拟基准：评估真实世界数据稀缺下跌倒检测的运动表示方法
translated_abstract: 跌倒是老年人面临的主要健康问题，可穿戴传感器已被广泛探索用于跌倒检测和及时干预。然而，现实世界中的跌倒极为罕见：收集100个跌倒样本需要估计约10万天的监测时间，导致用于训练机器学习模型的标记数据严重不足。因此，许多方法依赖模拟数据集，通常在实验室中表现良好，但现实世界的泛化能力有限。我们提出了一种在真实世界数据稀缺条件下，对可穿戴跌倒检测运动表示的系统性评估。利用加速度计信号，我们比较了基于区间、基于核、基于符号和基于基础模型的表示方法。作为可解释的基线，我们额外研究了一种轻量级符号表示，该表示将短运动片段转换为符号序列，并增强以物理基础的冲击描述符。实验结果表明……
tldr: 本文系统评估了多种运动表示方法在真实世界数据稀缺下的跌倒检测性能，并提出一种轻量级、可解释的符号表示方法，以提高泛化能力。
en_tdlr: This paper systematically evaluates motion representations for fall detection under real-world data scarcity and proposes a lightweight, interpretable symbolic representation to improve generalization.
